section_summary: Pages 161–190 conclude an illustrated Nagoya promotional booklet, covering the city’s industries, trade, transport, attractions, and chamber of commerce. The remaining pages concern invitations to Japanese exhibitions: a 1935 Osaka display of Dominican products, the proposed 1940 Tokyo International Exposition and its postponement, and a 1933 Tokyo exhibition on women and children.

subfiles.title: Illustrated promotional booklet on Nagoya
subfiles.from: Nagoya Chamber of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.about: Promotes Nagoya’s industrial output, port and rail facilities, foreign trade, visitor attractions, and commercial institutions.
subfiles.summary: The booklet traces Nagoya’s growth from a castle town into a major industrial center, emphasizing textile, engineering, pottery, food, and other manufactures. It gives production and trade tables through 1936 and describes rail, canal, harbor, air, and wireless links. Later pages present Nagoya Castle, shrines, parks, nearby resorts, the chamber of commerce, consulates, and hotels.

subfiles.title: Dominican products invited to Osaka Commercial Museum
subfiles.from: James S. Brown Jr., for the United States minister in Santo Domingo
subfiles.about: Reports the Santo Domingo Chamber of Commerce’s acceptance of an invitation to exhibit Dominican products in Osaka.
subfiles.summary: A newspaper reports that Dominican exhibits are being prepared for the March 15–April 4, 1935 exposition, intended to encourage Japan–Latin America trade.

subfiles.title: Duplicate of Santo Domingo despatch No. 2078
subfiles.about: Duplicates the report on Dominican participation in the Osaka Commercial Museum exposition.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the preceding despatch concerning Dominican exhibits for Osaka.

subfiles.title: Tokyo International Exposition case jacket
subfiles.about: Identifies the file on the proposed 1940 Tokyo International Exposition.
subfiles.summary: Jacket labels the 1940 Tokyo exposition case.

subfiles.title: Japanese invitation to the 1940 Tokyo International Exposition
subfiles.about: Invites United States government participation in the exposition commemorating Emperor Jimmu’s accession.
subfiles.summary: The ambassador promises a prospectus and supporting documents.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Japanese exposition invitation
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the invitation and awaits exposition documents before referring it to United States authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Department will consider the invitation after receiving the promised prospectus.

subfiles.title: Japanese transmittal of exposition prospectus
subfiles.about: Transmits the prospectus and other documents for the proposed Tokyo exposition.
subfiles.summary: The ambassador sends exposition planning documents.

subfiles.title: Grew asks about honorary exposition counselor role
subfiles.about: Requests instructions after being invited to serve as an honorary counselor for the Tokyo exposition.
subfiles.summary: Grew notes that some diplomatic colleagues have accepted similar roles.

subfiles.title: Embassy forwards exposition director’s letter
subfiles.about: Forwards G. Fujihara’s letter and informational documents on the 1940 exposition.
subfiles.summary: The Tokyo embassy transmits the exposition director’s communication and enclosures.

subfiles.title: Fujihara’s French letter seeking official participation
subfiles.about: Urges official United States participation in the Tokyo exposition and describes its commemorative aims.
subfiles.summary: Fujihara asks Grew to encourage a favorable United States response. He says the exposition will mark Emperor Jimmu’s 2,600th anniversary, promote understanding between civilizations, and receive imperial patronage.

subfiles.title: English translation of Fujihara’s letter
subfiles.about: Translates Fujihara’s request for United States representation at the Tokyo exposition.
subfiles.summary: Fujihara describes the exposition’s commemorative purpose, requests official participation, and promises revised abridged regulations.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs exposition chronology
subfiles.about: Summarizes the invitation, United States response, and later receipt of exposition materials.
subfiles.summary: Notes the exposition’s organizing association and the sequence of diplomatic exchanges.

subfiles.title: Instruction to decline honorary counselor appointment
subfiles.about: Advises Grew to decline the honorary exposition position absent substantial contrary reason.
subfiles.summary: Cites Department practice concerning honorary roles at expositions.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Tokyo exposition prospectus
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of exposition documents and says the invitation is under consideration.
subfiles.summary: The Department thanks Saito for the prospectus.

subfiles.title: Additional exposition documents and regulations
subfiles.about: Sends five more copies of exposition documents and extracts from its regulations.
subfiles.summary: Additional prospectus copies and regulations are enclosed.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of additional exposition documents
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Saito’s further Tokyo exposition materials.
subfiles.summary: The Department thanks the ambassador for the additional copies.

subfiles.title: Japanese exposition delegation visits Cuba
subfiles.from: Edward P. Lawton, for the ambassador in Habana
subfiles.about: Reports a Japanese mission’s invitation to Cuba to participate in the 1940 Tokyo exposition.
subfiles.summary: Local press says Cuba accepted. Lawton describes a banquet and judges the visit largely formal.

subfiles.title: Japanese exposition mission arrives in Brazil
subfiles.from: United States Embassy, Rio de Janeiro
subfiles.about: Reports a Japanese mission’s arrival to invite Brazilian participation in the Tokyo exposition.
subfiles.summary: The mission arrived by air on May 26; its members included Maruyama, Amari, and Ichikawa.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Uruguay exposition report
subfiles.about: Points to a report that a special mission would seek Uruguay’s participation.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to despatch No. 175 on Uruguay.

subfiles.title: Conversation on Philippine participation
subfiles.about: Records Yakichiro Suma’s proposal that the Philippine Islands participate as a special exposition unit.
subfiles.summary: Suma says the Japanese invitation did not expressly mention the Philippines. He suggests a separate unit, with a decision possible when the United States answers the main invitation.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Philippine participation memorandum
subfiles.about: Encloses the May 10 memorandum on proposed Philippine participation.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the conversation record to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Suma follows up on Philippine participation
subfiles.about: Records Suma’s inquiry about the proposed Philippine exposition unit.
subfiles.summary: Ballantine says consultation with other agencies and budget review will take time, and an answer will follow.

subfiles.title: Brazil announces intention to participate
subfiles.about: Reports President Vargas’s authorization of a statement that Brazil would join the Tokyo exposition.
subfiles.summary: João Maria de Lacerda announced Brazil’s intended participation.

subfiles.title: Japan postpones the 1940 exposition
subfiles.from: Counselor of the Japanese Embassy, for the ambassador
subfiles.about: Notifies the United States that the Tokyo International Exposition has been postponed.
subfiles.summary: Japan defers the exposition until a more appropriate time.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Brazil participation despatch
subfiles.about: Duplicates the report that Brazil intended to participate in the Tokyo exposition.
subfiles.summary: Copy of the Brazil participation announcement.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Cuba delegation despatch
subfiles.about: Duplicates the report on the Japanese exposition delegation’s Cuban visit.
subfiles.summary: Copy of the Habana report on Cuba’s reported acceptance and the mission’s formal visit.

subfiles.title: Japanese exposition mission visits Uruguay
subfiles.about: Reports the Japanese mission’s invitation to Uruguay and discussions with its leaders.
subfiles.summary: The mission arrived from Buenos Aires, met Foreign Minister Guani and President Baldomir, and discussed Uruguayan participation. Its visit also revived congressional discussion of the 1934 Japan–Uruguay commercial treaty.

subfiles.title: United States acknowledges exposition postponement
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Japan’s notification that the 1940 Tokyo exposition was postponed.
subfiles.summary: Formal receipt of the postponement notice.

subfiles.title: Advice to delay decision on Japanese invitation
subfiles.about: Recommends delaying a decision on participation amid uncertainty in the Far East.
subfiles.summary: Suggests postponing replies and interdepartmental consultation for several months.

subfiles.title: Policy and cost of United States exposition participation
subfiles.about: Seeks a Department policy decision before requesting agency views on participation in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Southgate anticipates a large appropriation and notes Japanese plans for the 1939 New York and San Francisco fairs. He considers delay feasible because the Tokyo exposition was scheduled for 1940.

subfiles.title: Women’s and Children’s International Exhibition case jacket
subfiles.about: Identifies the file for the planned 1933 Tokyo exhibition.
subfiles.summary: Jacket labels the women’s and children’s exhibition case.

subfiles.title: Grew forwards exhibition invitation and pamphlet
subfiles.about: Forwards Japan’s request for United States participation in the 1933 women’s and children’s exhibition.
subfiles.summary: Grew encloses a translated Foreign Office note and an exhibition pamphlet.

subfiles.title: Uchida requests United States participation
subfiles.about: Requests United States exhibits for the March–May 1933 exhibition in Ueno Park.
subfiles.summary: The organizers seek comparable material from foreign countries.

subfiles.title: Introduction to the Women’s and Children’s International Exhibition
subfiles.about: Explains the exhibition’s aims in women’s education, child welfare, household consumption, and international understanding.
subfiles.summary: The introduction calls for displays on food, clothing, housing, education, health, and hygiene. It presents the exhibition as a way to improve domestic consumption and encourage friendship among nations.

subfiles.title: General suggestions to foreign countries concerning exhibits
subfiles.from: Women’s and Children’s International Exhibition organizers
subfiles.about: Lists requested exhibit materials on women’s and children’s lives.
subfiles.summary: Requests household, educational, health, cultural, artistic, and photographic displays; the list continues beyond this section.
